original_text: add a ticket to audit and implement volk and cuda where and when possible.
context: Follows the question 'are we using cuda and volk acceleration?' (answer: no; all solvers are single-threaded double-precision CPU references; only acoustic analytical field evaluation is multithreaded). Machine: CUDA toolkit at /usr/local/cuda (nvcc), NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU (driver 595.99.02), VOLK 3.1 installed. Scope discussed: audit every compute path (acoustic FDTD, electromagnetic Yee FDTD, analytical field evaluation, array factor and pattern sampling, mechanics finite elements, signal processing / acquisition pipeline from request 008) for VOLK (SIMD signal-processing kernels) and CUDA (GPU) suitability; implement where it pays off, as optional backends selected at build and run time, with the CPU double-precision reference kept as fallback and accelerated results validated against it with the existing test tolerances (ADR-000205 CPU reference first; electromagnetics requirement: no dependence on one GPU vendor); CPU multithreading of the solvers considered as part of the audit; record precision, speedups and backend in result metadata; keep both CMake and qmake builds working when CUDA or VOLK are absent. Queued in order after the existing tickets.
